name: Zerona

card.summary: A low-level laser body-contouring system from Erchonia, used in clinics for non-surgical fat reduction around the waist, hips and thighs.
card.note: A small randomized split-body study found no statistically significant circumference reduction.

quick.overview:
Zerona is a cold, low-level laser treatment marketed for non-invasive fat reduction and body contouring, an alternative to liposuction. The FDA cleared it in 2010 as an infrared lamp, and the manufacturer describes light that makes fat cell membranes release stored fat.

The appearance goal is a slimmer waist, hips or thighs without surgery. Published evidence for the Zerona-branded device includes a small randomized study that reported no statistically significant circumference reduction.
quick.how: Treatment is clinic-based: a practitioner applies low-level laser to the target area over a series of sessions, a few times a week for a couple of weeks in the published trial. It is typically described alongside diet and exercise advice.
quick.risks: The treatment is non-invasive. Subjects in the small published trial rated the effects as less than they expected. Cost and the number of sessions vary by clinic.

lead: Zerona is a low-level laser system for non-surgical fat reduction, marketed as an alternative to liposuction. In 2010 the FDA cleared it for marketing as an infrared lamp [1]. Proponents say the laser light destabilises fat cell membranes so the cells release their stored fat without being destroyed [1].

In a small randomized split-body trial of the Erchonia EML laser, five subjects with BMI of 29 or less received laser treatment on one side of the body three times a week for two weeks. The authors reported no statistically significant circumference reduction at 7 days or one month, with the greatest reduction at one month being 0.5 inches, no significant ultrasound change in fat layer, and three subjects dissatisfied [2].
A T Nation forum user listed Zerona and CoolSculpting as alternatives to liposuction when asking about them [3].

paras: Zerona uses low-level laser therapy, sometimes called cold laser, to treat areas of stored fat without incision. The 2011 trial calls the device the Erchonia EML laser (Zerona system) [2].

The claimed action is that the light makes fat cell membranes less stable so cells release fat contents without being destroyed [1]. Low-level laser therapy has been reported to induce cellular reactions in non-photosynthetic cells, though the authors of the small trial note that skepticism remains about clinical efficacy [2].

A randomized, split-body trial in Lasers in Surgery and Medicine enrolled five subjects, with BMI 29 or less, who received laser on one side of the body three times a week for two weeks; one group also took a weight-loss supplement. Circumference measurements showed no statistically significant reduction at 7 days or 1 month, ultrasound did not show significant fat-layer reduction, three blinded dermatologists correctly identified photos 51.1 percent of the time, and subjects reported effects below expectations. Supplement users had no greater reduction. The authors concluded more evidence is needed before low-level laser can be recommended for circumferential reduction [2].
On T Nation a poster notes that the forum had no earlier threads on Zerona or CoolSculpting and presents them as non-surgical alternatives to liposuction [3].

timeline.event: FDA clears Zerona for marketing as an infrared lamp [1].
Small randomized split-body study of the Erchonia EML laser published [2].
